states.name: California
states.plan_mandate: Every city and county must adopt a general plan; charter cities must include its mandatory elements.
states.housing_duty: A housing element is mandatory under §65302(c), with detailed substantive requirements in §65583.
states.coverage: All cities and counties, including charter cities; no population cutoff.
states.allocation_detail: HCD determines regional need; councils of governments allocate municipal/county shares, or HCD does so where no council exists. Income-specific RHNA informs land capacity and programs, not a guarantee of construction. Seventh-cycle allocations separately identify acutely low and extremely low incomes.

contents.detail: Existing/projected need, household conditions, employment trends and special needs.
Needs and programs across income levels; seventh-cycle additions include acutely low income households.
Inventory of vacant and realistically redevelopable residential sites; relate zoning, services and fair housing to sites.
Identify adequate sites; rezone when inventory cannot accommodate assigned need.
Analyze governmental and market constraints and responses.
Fair-housing assessment, priorities, metrics and actions.
At-risk assisted housing and preservation programs.
Scheduled actions, responsible officials and quantified objectives.

Annual progress report due April 1 covers housing-element implementation, regional-need progress, applications, approvals, entitlements, permits, occupancy and rezoned sites. Additional replacement/demolition reporting begins with the April 1, 2027 report.

states.enforcement: HCD reviews drafts and adopted elements, may revoke compliance findings and refer violations to the Attorney General; courts can order compliance and impose escalating remedies under §65585.
states.key_distinction: RHNA is an external allocation of planning need. Quantified program objectives may differ from total need (§65583(b)(2)); this does not eliminate the adequate-sites obligation.

evidence.reasoning: Universal plan-adoption duty plus mandatory housing element.
Express county/city coverage, including charter cities; no size trigger.
Regional determination becomes each locality's assigned share and housing-element input.
Administrative review and court remedies address planning compliance.
Section65400 requires an annual public progress report including housing-program compliance and development milestones, with state correction requests and court compliance orders.

Section65584(b)(1) assigns regional need determination to HCD; subsection(b)(2) separately assigns municipal apportionment. Section65583(a)(1) requires local analysis to include that share. The actor code follows the controlling regional calculation, not authorship of the element.

states.assessment_detail: California HCD determines each region’s existing and projected housing need in consultation with its council of governments. Cities and counties separately assess local housing conditions and needs in their elements, but that local analysis must include the allocated regional share.
states.assessment_method: The statutory RHNA process governs HCD’s regional determination and the subsequent allocation, with statutory allocation objectives. Section 65583 prescribes the separate local assessment of population, employment, household characteristics, special needs and constraints.
states.assessment_local_role: The locality prepares and adopts its housing element, quantifies local needs and identifies sites and programs to accommodate its regional share. Local diagnosis does not replace the external RHNA number.
states.allocation_authority: Councils of governments; HCD where no COG

states.name: Texas
states.plan_mandate: A municipality may adopt a comprehensive plan and determines its contents and its relationship to development regulations.
states.housing_duty: No express municipal housing element duty in Chapter 213. A municipality can include housing by local choice.
states.coverage: General municipal planning authority statewide; no population cutoff for a housing component appears in Chapter 213.
states.allocation_detail: Chapter 213 delegates plan contents to municipalities; it neither calculates statewide housing need nor apportions units to individual municipalities.
states.enforcement: Chapter 213 provides public hearing and planning-department/commission review procedures for adopted plans; no housing-element certification or housing allocation enforcement appears there.
states.key_distinction: Optional comprehensive planning is only one reason for this code: the operative content provisions themselves leave housing unspecified. This is not a conclusion about every HUD, land-bank, or housing-finance program.

evidence.reasoning: Section 213.002(a) delegates content and design; (b) gives nonexclusive optional subjects and does not require housing.
Chapter 213 is a general municipal authorization without a housing-specific class trigger.
No allocating entity, municipal share, or mandatory unit count appears in the reviewed chapter.
The cited planning or housing-plan provisions support the stated procedure and scoped enforcement finding; no unit-production guarantee is inferred.
Read §213.002’s operative delegation of content/design and optional topics: it assigns general plan choices to the municipality but no housing-need estimation duty to a state or local assessor.

states.assessment_detail: Chapter 213 identifies no required municipal housing-need estimate or institution responsible for producing one. Its local comprehensive-plan authorization does not establish that cities actually assess housing need.
states.assessment_method: The municipality defines plan content and design under §213.002; Chapter 213 prescribes no housing-need formula, dataset or state-calculated planning total.
states.assessment_local_role: A municipality may choose to study housing in its plan. The reviewed chapter requires neither that optional analysis nor accommodation of an externally assigned housing number.

states.name: Florida
states.plan_mandate: Each local government must maintain a comprehensive plan; a new municipality must adopt one within three years of incorporation.
states.housing_duty: The comprehensive plan must contain a housing element.
states.coverage: Incorporated municipalities and counties; no population cutoff for housing. The county plan controls a newly incorporated municipality until its own plan is adopted.
states.allocation_detail: Local housing-needs analysis derives household projections by income, size and age from population projections. State demographic data and a county-proportional growth floor constrain planning, but the reviewed sections do not allocate regional housing-unit need to each municipality.

contents.detail: Housing stock, condition, tenure, costs and cost burdens; projected households and minimum current/future housing need.
Adequate sites for workforce, very-low-, low- and moderate-income housing and special housing types.
Substandard conditions, rehabilitation, historic housing and preservation of affordability.
Housing programs; partnerships, streamlined permitting and reduced affordable-housing costs/delays.
Adequate future housing sites and infrastructure are required, but this is not an express parcel-by-parcel sites inventory.

states.enforcement: The plan must specify monitoring and implementation procedures. This inventory codes planning duties, not a guarantee of housing construction.
states.key_distinction: Housing-unit needs are locally analyzed; the state population-projection framework is not California's income-specific municipal allocation system.

evidence.reasoning: Plan maintenance is compulsory; housing appears in the mandatory elements.
Section 163.3167 covers municipalities and counties and provides the incorporation transition.
Subsections (1)(f) and (6)(f) prescribe population inputs and local needs analysis, without an external municipal housing-unit assignment.
Section (1)(d) requires plan monitoring procedures; (5)(b) and (6)(f) require implementation policies and programs. No production guarantee is inferred.

Section 163.3177(6)(f)2 requires the housing analysis within the local element. Section (1)(f)2–3 regulates acceptable data/methods and population baselines, rather than making the state the housing-needs assessor.

states.assessment_detail: Each local government prepares or commissions the housing-needs analysis for current and future residents, including projected households by size, income and age. State population projections are inputs, not a state housing-needs assessment assigned to the city.
states.assessment_method: Section 163.3177 specifies housing data and requires professionally accepted methods. Population projections may come from the Office of Economic and Demographic Research or a professionally acceptable local method; state medium projections set a minimum land-accommodation baseline, with proportional county-growth safeguards.
states.assessment_local_role: Translate demographic projections into local household and housing needs and adopt the housing element. The state-data and growth-floor requirements constrain inputs but do not supply a California-style municipal housing-unit allocation.

states.name: New York
states.plan_mandate: General city, town and village enabling statutes expressly encourage, but do not require, preparation and adoption of a comprehensive plan.
states.housing_duty: Existing housing resources and future housing needs, including affordable housing, are expressly optional plan topics.
states.coverage: General City Law §28-a applies to cities with population no greater than one million and excludes New York City. Town Law §272-a and Village Law §7-722 apply to those municipal types. NYC's local charter planning is a separate regime, not a general statewide housing-element mandate.
states.allocation_detail: The reviewed city, town and village planning statutes do not assign municipal housing-unit need. They permit consideration of regional needs and local housing resources.

contents.detail: Existing housing resources and future need, including affordability, may be included.
Optional measures/programs to carry out plan objectives.

states.enforcement: Once adopted, municipal land-use regulations must accord with the plan; adoption also triggers procedural review. These effects do not make the optional housing topic mandatory.
states.key_distinction: A mandatory zoning-consistency rule is different from a duty to adopt a housing element. S2084 remained in Assembly committee when checked.

evidence.reasoning: Plan adoption is expressly encouraged, and housing appears under may include.
The city statute contains the one-million exclusion; separate statutes cover towns and villages.

states.assessment_method: No mandatory housing-needs calculation method appears in these optional comprehensive-plan provisions. This finding does not imply that state housing research or voluntary local studies do not exist.
states.assessment_local_role: Local legislative/planning bodies may include housing analysis in an optional plan; that discretion is not coded as a mandatory local assessment. The general city provision excludes cities over one million.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.plan_mandate: Municipalities governed by the Municipalities Planning Code may adopt a comprehensive plan. Counties have a separate adoption duty.
states.housing_duty: A municipal, multimunicipal or county comprehensive plan must include a plan to meet present and anticipated residents' housing needs.
states.coverage: Municipalities under the MPC: cities of second class A and third class, boroughs, incorporated towns and townships. The MPC does not govern first- and second-class cities (Philadelphia and Pittsburgh); their special regimes are outside this classification.
states.allocation_detail: The MPC requires assessment of present and anticipated local residents. Joint plans may accommodate uses across the participating area; the reviewed MPC provisions do not create state-assigned municipal housing-need numbers.

contents.detail: Housing/demographic/economic studies and a plan for present/future housing needs.
Housing types and densities across incomes are listed as permissible means of addressing need.
Conservation of sound housing and rehabilitation of declining neighborhoods are illustrative optional measures.
Discuss short- and long-range implementation strategies.

states.enforcement: Public adoption and county/neighbor consultation; plans generally guide decisions. Section 303(c) bars invalidating an action solely for inconsistency with the plan.
states.key_distinction: The housing component is compulsory in an adopted comprehensive plan, while municipal plan adoption itself is generally permissive under the MPC.

evidence.reasoning: Section 302 says may adopt; §301(a)(2.1) lists required housing content.
The act's scope excludes first- and second-class cities and separately requires county plans in §301.4.
Sections 301, 301.2 and 1103 frame local/regional planning without an external municipal housing-unit allocation.
Sections 301.3 and 302 prescribe consultation/adoption; §303(c) expressly limits inconsistency-based challenges.

Section 301.2 assigns studies to the planning agency; §1103(a) expressly permits municipal or county-prepared regional plans covering the housing needs of the plan area. That legal choice supports local_or_regional.

states.assessment_method: MPC §§301(a)(2.1), 301.2 and 1103 require housing-needs planning and surveys of housing, demographic and economic trends. No state numerical housing-needs formula was identified in these provisions; county consistency and consultation requirements still apply.
states.assessment_local_role: A municipality electing to plan, or participating in a multimunicipal plan, develops the needs analysis individually or cooperatively and adopts the resulting plan. Joint regional housing analysis is distinct from a state-imposed municipal allocation.
states.allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified

states.name: Illinois
states.plan_mandate: The Affordable Housing Planning and Appeal Act imposes a separate affordable housing plan regardless of whether the municipality elects a comprehensive plan.
states.housing_duty: Non-exempt local governments must adopt an affordable housing plan. Newly non-exempt governments have 18 months after IHDA notification.
states.coverage: Municipalities with population at least 1,000 and less than 10% affordable year-round housing, as determined by IHDA; counties also covered. Municipalities under 1,000 or with at least 10% affordable housing are exempt.
states.allocation_detail: IHDA calculates existing affordable-stock percentages. The plan selects one or more statutory goals: 15% of new development/redevelopment affordable, a 5-percentage-point increase in affordable stock, or 10% overall affordable stock. These are uniform statutory benchmarks with local choice, not an allocation of regional housing need to cities.

contents.detail: State the affordable units needed to reach exempt status.
Affordability calculations distinguish owner units affordable below 80% and rental units below 60% of median household income in the county or primary metropolitan statistical area.

Identify suitable land for affordable construction and structures suitable for conversion or rehabilitation; consider ownership/rental, committed developers, and public or semi-public sites. Not the detailed California parcel-capacity protocol.
Describe market conditions, infrastructure limits, ordinances and policies constraining affordable housing; devise mitigation strategies.
Constraints analysis includes policies or practices that fail to affirmatively further fair housing.
Identify incentives, choose statutory goal(s), and propose timelines for actions to commence within 24 months of adoption.
File the plan with IHDA within 60 days; implementation report no later than four years after adoption/update; prior plans require progress summaries.

states.enforcement: IHDA determines substantial compliance and notifies violations; the Attorney General may seek mandamus, injunction, or other relief. Section 30 also provides affordable-development appeals. These mechanisms do not guarantee unit production.
states.key_distinction: The Act’s encouragement language in its purpose does not make the non-exempt-government duty optional. Its 10% exemption threshold and alternative goals are not California-style regional need allocation.

evidence.reasoning: Section 25(a) expressly requires all non-exempt governments to approve a plan.
Read exempt-local-government definition together with IHDA calculation and notification provisions; a municipality at exactly 1,000 is not population-exempt.
IHDA’s arithmetic measures existing affordability; § 25(b)(vi) gives alternative uniform goals rather than dividing a regional need total.
The cited planning or housing-plan provisions support the stated procedure and scoped enforcement finding; no unit-production guarantee is inferred.

Section 20 explicitly makes IHDA the existing-stock/exemption calculator. Section 25(b)(i) requires the locally adopted plan to state the affordable units necessary for exemption, with local implementation and alternative statutory goals. This is a stock benchmark rather than a housing-demand estimate: no forward-looking housing-needs assessment or forecast is identified in the reviewed AHPAA planning regime. The benchmark_only classification preserves the separate IHDA/local roles without treating them as a state-and-local forecast of housing need.

A non-exempt local government’s plan must state the affordable units necessary to reach exemption and address local constraints and implementation. This is a stock/exemption benchmark, not a state forecast of total or regional future housing need.
states.assessment_method: Sections 15 and 20 prescribe IHDA’s formula using Census and other relevant data: affordable owner units below 80% and rental units below 60% of county or metropolitan median household income, divided by total year-round housing units. Section 25 requires the local plan’s exemption-unit statement and supplies alternative statutory goals. IHDA’s additional income-band data are informational and do not determine exemptions.
states.assessment_local_role: The local government adopts the affordable housing plan, states its exemption-related unit requirement using the statutory benchmark, identifies sites/constraints/incentives, and chooses one or more §25 goals. It can appeal IHDA’s exemption determination under the Act; it receives no allocated share of regional future need.
states.allocation_authority: No regional-need allocator; statutory stock benchmarks

states.name: Ohio
states.plan_mandate: Section 713.01 authorizes cities and villages to establish commissions. Once established, § 713.02 directs the commission to make plans and maps.
states.housing_duty: The reviewed municipal planning statute does not expressly require a housing element, housing needs assessment, or equivalent citywide housing plan.
states.coverage: General city/village planning-commission regime; no housing-specific population or geography trigger appears in §§ 713.01–.02. Local charter provisions may add duties.
states.allocation_detail: The enumerated planning duties and public-project review powers in § 713.02 do not allocate state or regional housing need to municipalities.
states.enforcement: The statute requires commission review of specified public projects after a plan exists, with legislative overrides. No housing-element compliance or assigned-unit enforcement mechanism is identified in these provisions.
states.key_distinction: A duty to make municipal plans is not itself a duty to prepare a housing element; a local housing strategy or federal consolidated plan is a different instrument.

evidence.reasoning: Examined the mandatory list of plan/map recommendations: public ways, grounds, buildings and utilities, without a housing-needs component.
General city/village authorization and duties contain no housing-element trigger.
The statute concerns municipal physical planning and contains no quantified municipal housing shares or assigning state/regional body.
The cited planning or housing-plan provisions support the stated procedure and scoped enforcement finding; no unit-production guarantee is inferred.

The institution named in §713.02 is a local planning commission, but its enumerated duties do not include housing-need estimation. General planning responsibility therefore does not justify coding a local housing assessor.

states.assessment_method: The statute lists physical/public-facility planning topics and permits information and funding cooperation. It supplies no housing-demand calculation method or state housing total for municipal planning.
states.assessment_local_role: The commission performs the statutory general planning work. A municipality’s voluntary housing study is not established by that general duty; no external housing-unit number must be accommodated under the reviewed sections.

states.name: Georgia
states.plan_mandate: A comprehensive plan is required to retain qualified-local-government certification and eligibility for selected state funding and permitting programs.
states.housing_duty: Housing element required for HUD Community Development Block Grant Entitlement Communities; expressly optional and encouraged for other local governments.
states.coverage: The operative trigger is HUD CDBG entitlement-community status, not receipt of any federal grant. The standards operate within Georgia's qualified-local-government planning system; approved alternative planning requirements are possible.
states.allocation_detail: Evaluate local housing-stock adequacy and current/future needs. The reviewed rules prescribe no state or regional assignment of a municipal housing-unit share.

contents.detail: Evaluate housing mix, condition, occupancy, costs, cost-burdened households and jobs–housing balance.
Affordability/cost burdens, special populations and housing across the life cycle.
Integrate housing-related goals, needs/opportunities and work-program actions into the comprehensive plan even when using a Consolidated Plan analysis.

states.enforcement: Regional Commission and Department of Community Affairs review for conformity; certification determines eligibility for selected funding and permitting programs.
states.key_distinction: The required analysis inventories existing housing stock; it does not prescribe a parcel-level inventory of developable sites.

evidence.reasoning: Rules .02 and .03(9) expressly distinguish mandatory CDBG entitlement communities from other governments.
The housing row in .02 and .03(9) provides the HUD entitlement trigger; .02 explains qualified-government eligibility and alternatives.
The housing analytical factors concern local adequacy; the reviewed rules contain no external municipal unit allocation.
Rule .02 links planning compliance to qualified-local-government eligibility and describes state/regional review.

Rule .03(9) directs the local housing evaluation and permits substitution of existing local/consolidated analysis. Rule .04 provides external review, without assigning the state or regional commission the city's need calculation.

sources.supports: Trigger, planning certification, housing analytical factors and work-program integration.

states.assessment_detail: For the CDBG entitlement communities required to include housing, the local comprehensive-plan process evaluates housing-stock adequacy for current and future community needs. Existing consolidated-plan or comparable local housing-plan analysis may substitute.
states.assessment_method: DCA Rule 110-12-1-.03(9) prescribes factors including stock/type/condition, costs and burdens, jobs-housing balance, special populations and life-cycle options. The reviewed rule does not prescribe a state-calculated unit-need total.
states.assessment_local_role: Prepare or incorporate the local housing analysis and integrate applicable goals, needs and work-program items into the comprehensive plan. Regional/state review of that plan is not the same as calculating and allocating municipal housing need.
states.allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified

states.name: North Carolina
states.plan_mandate: A local government must adopt and reasonably maintain a comprehensive or land-use plan as a condition of exercising zoning authority.
states.housing_duty: Housing plans and a comprehensive-plan topic covering diverse housing types and affordability are expressly optional under the general enabling statute.
states.coverage: General framework applies to local governments exercising Chapter 160D zoning authority; no population trigger for the optional housing topic. Coastal CAMA land-use planning has additional rules and is treated separately in the caveat.
states.allocation_detail: The reviewed general planning statute creates no state/regional allocation of municipal housing-unit need.

contents.detail: A plan may address housing types and affordability for all household types and income levels.
Optional separate housing plan and general needs analysis.

states.enforcement: Adoption is a condition of zoning authority. Plans are advisory without independent regulatory effect, and must be considered when amending zoning.
states.key_distinction: Mandatory adoption of some plan does not make every suggested topic mandatory. Coastal land-use rules additionally require housing-stock information; stock description is not a housing-needs allocation.

evidence.reasoning: Section (a) mandates a plan for zoning, while (a1) and (b) make housing plans/topics permissive.
The general trigger is zoning under Chapter 160D, not population.
Review of Article 5 found optional housing content and planning coordination, but no externally assigned municipal unit count.
Section (a) conditions zoning on planning, while (c) makes plans advisory and requires consideration in rezoning.
Section 160D-501(a1),(b)(5) makes housing plans/topics discretionary, while (c) governs local adoption. It does not require an estimate or allocate an assessor.

states.assessment_method: The reviewed general-planning statute sets no mandatory housing-need calculation method. Its optional housing topic concerns types and affordability; the separate coastal stock-inventory access caveat remains.
states.assessment_local_role: A local government may undertake housing analysis within its plan, which is adopted with planning-board advice. That optional analysis is not treated as a state-mandated local need assessment.
states.allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified

states.name: Michigan
states.plan_mandate: The Planning Enabling Act authorizes a local government to adopt a master plan and create a planning commission; once constituted, the commission shall make and approve a plan. This is not a universal municipal housing-element mandate.
states.housing_duty: Master plans must include an assessment of existing and forecast housing demands, with responsive strategies and policies, among subjects reasonably pertinent to future development. This express housing provision took effect April 2, 2025.
states.coverage: No population cutoff in the housing provision. Applies through the master-plan framework and its pertinence qualification. Plans carried forward from repealed planning acts are exempt from §33 contents until first amended under the 2008 act.
states.allocation_detail: The statute calls for an assessment of the community's own housing demands. No state or regional assignment of municipal unit needs was identified in the reviewed Planning Enabling Act.

contents.detail: Assess existing and forecast community housing demands, subject to the statutory pertinence qualification.
Strategies and policies to address those demands; the plan also includes implementation recommendations.
Review the master plan at least every five years and record whether amendment or replacement should begin; this is plan review rather than a housing-production reporting duty.

states.enforcement: The act prescribes plan adoption, intergovernmental notice and periodic review. No housing-specific state certification, assigned unit quota or housing-production sanction was identified in this act.
states.key_distinction: Michigan now expressly requires a housing-demand assessment in applicable master plans; a claim that its planning act is silent on housing misses the 2025-effective amendment.

evidence.reasoning: Sections 7 and 11 authorize planning; §31 makes plan preparation a commission duty, and §33(2)(e) expressly adds housing demands and policies.
Section 33 uses a pertinence qualification without a size threshold; §81(1) preserves an exception for certain unamended older plans.
Section 33 assigns the assessment to the community's plan and supplies no external allocation formula or municipal fair-share assignment.
The reviewed act prescribes adoption, notice and five-year review; no housing-specific certification or output sanction was identified in that act.

Sections31 and33 place plan preparation and the housing-demand assessment with the planning commission. State legislation specifies this local assessment duty; it does not itself calculate the community’s housing demand.

states.assessment_detail: The local planning commission prepares the master plan, including an assessment of the community’s existing and forecast housing demands and responsive policies, subject to the statutory pertinence qualification and older-plan exception.

states.name: Oregon

contents.detail: Analyze the municipality's additional moderate-income housing needs for the next five years and realistic opportunities to meet them.
The element focuses on moderate-income housing, defined as affordable at 80% of county median gross household income, adjusted for household size.

Without a fixed-guideway station: select at least three listed strategies, or at least one of the special housing-zone/density-bonus strategies (X)–(CC). With a station: five including station-area planning and specified transit-density or parking reform, or the alternative three-strategy combination. Adopt a five-year implementation timeline with specific benchmarks.

Specified municipalities report implementation actions and barriers, ADUs, entitlements, building permits, occupancy and zoning information. The ordinary report is due August 1; 2026 has a statutory reporting pause and carryover compliance, with a separate July 1 occupancy-count requirement.
Strategies can address zoning, fees, parking, infrastructure and approvals; no single reform is universally required because municipalities choose among statutory alternatives.

states.enforcement: State review determines compliance and allows cure and appeal. Noncompliance can cause specified transportation-funding ineligibility and daily fees; the statute also authorizes injunctive enforcement. The 2026 reporting pause preserves qualifying 2025 compliance; normal implementation reporting resumes in 2027.

states.name: Kansas
states.plan_mandate: A city may create a planning commission, which is authorized to prepare and adopt a comprehensive plan subject to governing-body approval. §12-747 prescribes surveys, recommendations, hearings and annual review when a plan is prepared; it does not require every city to adopt one.
states.housing_duty: No express housing element or standing equivalent municipal housing-policy plan was identified in the reviewed general planning statutes. Required plan surveys and residential land-use recommendations are broader than a housing-needs element. A separate community needs analysis is required before voluntarily creating a Reinvestment Housing Incentive District.
states.coverage: The general municipal planning framework applies without a housing-specific population cutoff. The separate district program is open to city or county governing bodies; it concerns selected housing-development districts, not a statewide general-plan housing requirement.
states.allocation_detail: No external municipal housing-need allocation is specified in the general planning framework. In the separate district financing program, the Secretary of Commerce reviews the locality’s shortage findings but does not assign a municipal share of statewide or regional need.
states.assessment_detail: §12-747 does not expressly require a housing-demand estimate or designate a housing-need assessor. Separately, §12-5244 does require the city/county governing body to conduct a community housing-needs analysis before creating an incentive district, with state concurrence in its findings; that project-financing pathway is outside the general-plan classification.
states.assessment_method: General-plan surveys cover land use, population/building intensity, facilities, transport, economic conditions and natural resources. For the separate incentive-district analysis, state law requires findings about quality housing shortages across price ranges, persistence, economic effects and need for incentives; the locality conducts the analysis and the Secretary reviews those findings.
states.assessment_local_role: The local commission prepares general-plan surveys and recommendations. A locality electing an incentive district separately analyzes its community’s housing needs and adopts a district development/feasibility plan after state concurrence; it receives no externally apportioned unit obligation.
states.enforcement: For a comprehensive plan, §12-747 requires a hearing, governing-body approval, publication and at least annual commission review. No housing-element certification or omission penalty is identified there. The separate incentive-district program requires Secretary of Commerce concurrence in shortage findings before proceeding and a local development plan/hearing.
states.key_distinction: The general-plan finding is scoped: Kansas does require an actual local community housing-needs analysis for voluntary incentive districts. State review of that analysis is not state assessment or fair-share allocation, and the district project plan is not treated as a standing municipal housing element.

evidence.reasoning: Optional planning authority is read together with the complete required surveys/plan-content list; no express housing element appears.
The general city framework has no housing cutoff; the separate elective district program is disclosed and kept outside the standing municipal-plan scope.
No housing-demand estimate is expressly mandated for the comprehensive plan. The distinct district statute does assign community analysis to the local governing body, subject to state concurrence.
Neither general-plan recommendations nor state review of local shortage findings apportions statewide/regional housing need to municipalities.
General local adoption/review procedures and district-specific state concurrence are identified separately.
District financing analysis/plan duties prevent interpreting the general-plan negative as absence of all state-imposed housing assessments.

When adopted, the statutory comprehensive plan must contain the minimum components defined in §17-1-1(c). The reviewed provisions do not direct every municipality to adopt a plan independently of that framework.
states.housing_duty: Housing must be included in the community-facilities plan that forms a basis for a capital-improvements program. The comprehensive plan also requires long-range residential-development goals and a residential land-use distribution/density description. This is a narrow required housing topic, not a separately specified housing-needs element.
states.coverage: The comprehensive-plan definition covers the entire municipality or county; municipality includes any incorporated city, town or village. No population cutoff appears. Coverage is conditional on the comprehensive-planning/zoning framework rather than a universal municipal housing-plan adoption command.
states.allocation_detail: No state or regional housing-unit apportionment to municipalities is specified in the reviewed minimum-plan and zoning-conformity provisions. Optional use of population/economic projections to inform land-use recommendations is not an assigned municipal housing share.
states.assessment_detail: The statutory minimum housing topic does not require a quantified housing-demand estimate or identify a state, regional or local institution that must produce one. Population and economic-growth projections may inform quantitative land-use recommendations, but are not a mandatory housing-needs calculation.
states.assessment_method: §17-1-1(c) identifies planning topics and permits demographic/economic projections as a basis for land-use recommendations; no housing-needs formula or required forecasting methodology is specified there.
states.assessment_local_role: The local governing body adopts the comprehensive plan and its community-facilities/housing topic. The reviewed minimum-content provisions assign no external unit number to be accommodated.

contents.detail: Housing is an express item in the community-facilities plan; long-range goals must address residential development and the land-use plan must describe residential distribution and densities. Generic land-use mapping is not treated as a parcel inventory of housing sites.
The community-facilities plan, including housing, is to serve as a basis for a capital-improvements program. No housing-specific action schedule or production quota is stated.

states.enforcement: The identified statutory connection is that zoning regulations must be made in accordance with a comprehensive plan. The reviewed minimum-content provisions do not establish state housing-element certification, a housing-specific periodic update, or a sanction for missing a housing-unit target.
states.key_distinction: An express housing topic exists even though the statute lacks the detailed housing-element machinery found elsewhere. A required community-facilities item does not by itself mandate a needs forecast, sites inventory or fair-share allocation.

evidence.reasoning: Minimum comprehensive-plan components expressly include housing in the community-facilities/capital-improvements topic; zoning must accord with a plan.
Definition includes all incorporated cities/towns/villages without a size threshold; discretionary zoning authority and plan conformity frame the conditional duty.
Read the entire minimum-content definition: housing is a facilities topic, and population/economic projections are permissive. No mandatory housing-demand estimate or assessor is named.
The adopted local policy/content requirements do not identify state/regional totals, a formula, or a municipal allocating authority.
The reviewed mechanism is zoning-plan conformity; no housing-unit target or certification mechanism appears in these sections.

states.name: New Mexico
states.plan_mandate: A county or municipality using the Affordable Housing Act to make housing-assistance grants/donations must have an existing valid affordable-housing plan or housing elements within its general plan. This is a standing community housing strategy, which may be separate from the comprehensive plan.
states.housing_duty: An adopted affordable-housing plan, reviewed by Housing New Mexico/Mortgage Finance Authority (MFA), is a prerequisite for local Affordable Housing Act donations. Rule 4.1 specifies community-wide needs, land-use analysis and goals, subject to feasibility and readily available data.
states.coverage: Counties and municipalities making housing-assistance grants under the Affordable Housing Act, with no population cutoff. Grants include land, buildings and housing/infrastructure costs; participation is the trigger. The municipal definition includes incorporated cities, towns and villages and specified incorporated/H-class counties.
states.allocation_detail: Local governments prepare their own estimates of existing and projected need and unit objectives; they may jointly plan with needs disaggregated for each participant. MFA approves plan/ordinance compliance but does not assign an external municipal fair-share number under the reviewed Act and rules.
states.assessment_detail: The participating county or municipality prepares a housing-needs assessment, either individually or through an optional joint county/municipal plan addressing each entity’s needs.
states.assessment_method: MFA Rule 4.1 requires demographic/market analysis, cost-burden/overcrowding/special-needs measures, AMI affordability gaps and projected units by tenure, type and cost. Required elements are qualified by feasibility and readily available data; no state-apportioned unit formula is specified.
states.assessment_local_role: The local governing body adopts the plan and housing ordinance. A joint plan must disaggregate data and recommendations. MFA reviews compliance; locality/joint planners generate the needs estimates and quantified objectives.
states.allocation_authority: No external allocator identified; MFA reviews compliance

contents.detail: Community/housing profile; existing cost burden, overcrowding and special needs; projected units by tenure, type and cost for current need, population growth and jobs. Rule 4.1 applies when feasible and data are readily available.
Identify housing-cost/income gaps by AMI and unit objectives by income levels, subject to the Rule 4.1 feasibility/data qualifier.

Analyze land-use parcels by zoning, size, use, environmental constraints and infrastructure; evaluate suitability and availability of developable sites. This is site analysis, not an expressly prescribed parcel-table format; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.
Evaluate realistic development capacity of developable sites, appropriate special-needs housing zoning and minimum affordable-housing density calculations; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.
Identify regulatory, permit, fee, infrastructure, financing, land-price, construction-cost and local administrative constraints; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.
Identify programs/agencies promoting access and equal opportunity to affordable housing, including assistance for people with disabilities; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.
Determine homes to be created through construction, rehabilitation and preservation, with quantifiable objectives; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.
Quantifiable time-period objectives, responsible programs/agencies, incentives to remove constraints and potential financing sources; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.

states.enforcement: MFA reviews plans and enabling ordinances; the local governing body must adopt/pass them. Proposed ordinances must be submitted at least 45 days before enactment under § 6-27-7. Rule 4.2 makes failure to submit required documents or comply with an invalidity determination invalidate the ordinance and acts under it. These controls condition donations, not universal local housing production.
states.key_distinction: The law requires a standing adopted community housing plan as a donation prerequisite, not merely a project financing plan. State approval of locally produced need estimates is different from state allocation.

evidence.reasoning: Section 6-27-8(C)(11) expressly requires an existing valid plan/housing element for counties/municipalities making grants; Rule 4.1 establishes substantive community-wide content.
The trigger is local Affordable Housing Act grants, not population or receipt of a generalized state planning mandate.
The local plan contains the need analysis; official guidance permits joint plans with disaggregated local needs. MFA reviews adequacy, rather than calculating controlling municipal shares.
Locally generated projected needs and objectives are required, with joint planning permitted, but no externally assigned municipal number in the reviewed regime.
Section 6-27-7 and Rule 4 establish prior state review, local adoption and consequences for invalid ordinances.

states.name: Idaho
states.plan_mandate: Every city and county must exercise the Local Land Use Planning Act powers. The planning commission, or governing board exercising its powers, prepares, implements, reviews and updates a comprehensive plan.
states.housing_duty: Housing is a listed mandatory comprehensive-plan component, subject to the express exception allowing the plan to explain why a particular component is unneeded.
states.coverage: All cities and counties; no population threshold. Section 67-6508 permits omission of a component when the plan specifies why it is unneeded. County jurisdiction is over unincorporated territory.
states.allocation_detail: The local planning body analyzes housing conditions and community needs. No state or regional assignment of a quantified municipal share was identified in the reviewed Local Land Use Planning Act provisions.
states.assessment_detail: The city or county planning commission, or governing board acting in its place, conducts the housing-conditions and needs analysis.
states.assessment_method: State law specifies subjects, including population trends and housing conditions, but the reviewed sections prescribe no statewide housing-unit formula.
states.assessment_local_role: The locality prepares and adopts the analysis and housing provisions; it may explain why a component is unneeded. No externally assigned housing number was identified.

Plan improvements to housing standards and safe, sanitary, adequate housing, including manufactured/mobile-home siting sufficient to maintain competitive markets. General implementation component covers actions, programs, budgets, ordinances and expenditure schedules.
General land-use analysis maps suitable projected uses, including housing. It is not an express inventory of available housing parcels.

states.enforcement: Plans and amendments require commission hearing procedures and governing-board adoption by resolution. The reviewed sections establish local planning duties and adoption procedures, without an identified state housing-element certification or assigned-unit enforcement process.
states.key_distinction: Housing is presumptively required statewide, but a locality may expressly justify omitting a component as unneeded; this is not an unconditional housing-element mandate.

Every city and county is covered; governing-board/commission alternatives and the omission exception do not create a population cutoff.
The local planning body has the duty to analyze housing conditions and needs; enumerated state topics do not make the state the assessor.

states.name: Nebraska
states.plan_mandate: The Municipal Density and Missing Middle Housing Act requires covered cities to adopt an affordable housing action plan, either within the comprehensive plan or as a separate plan. Thus its housing duty does not depend on an optional decision to adopt a general plan.
states.housing_duty: Covered cities must adopt an affordable housing action plan and submit biennial affordable-housing reports. The action-plan deadline was January 1, 2023 for cities of at least 50,000 and January 1, 2024 for smaller covered cities.
states.coverage: “City” means a metropolitan-class city, primary-class city, or first-class city with at least 20,000 inhabitants, determined by the most recent federal decennial census or revised certified Census Bureau count. The under-50,000 deadline does not extend the act to every small municipality.
states.allocation_detail: Each covered city estimates housing need and sets its own construction and zoning goals. No state/regional housing need apportioned among cities appears in §§19-5503–5505; the legislative committee receives reports rather than assigning unit shares.
states.assessment_detail: Each covered city must report a demographic analysis with trends and estimated housing need by housing type and price range. This is a city-produced estimate accompanying the affordable housing action-plan regime.
states.assessment_method: State law prescribes demographic trends and type/price-range categories for the estimate, but these provisions provide no statewide forecasting or municipal-share formula. The affordable-housing definition references HUD income limits as they existed January 1, 2022; that definition does not make HUD or the state the need assessor.
states.assessment_local_role: The city prepares the need analysis, adopts numerical construction and zoning goals, selects incentives and zoning updates, and reports to the Legislature’s Urban Affairs Committee.

contents.detail: Biennial report must include demographic trends and estimates of housing need classified by housing type and price range.
The action plan addresses affordable, middle and workforce housing. Affordable housing is defined using the statutory 80-percent income-limit standard; report estimates are classified by price range.
Construction goals must identify types, numbers and geographic locations of new units; this is not an express parcel-by-parcel developable-site inventory.
Plan must include actions to encourage construction, goals for the percentage of residential areas allowing multifamily/middle housing, incentive plans, and zoning updates.
Biennial July 1 reports beginning 2021 cover zoning, construction and annexation over the prior five years, costs, incentives, blighted areas and action-plan progress.

states.enforcement: Cities must transmit adopted plans and biennial reports to the Urban Affairs Committee, which may require a public presentation. Failure to adopt the required action plan triggers a duty to permit middle housing in residential areas allowing detached single-family dwellings and a duplex on every such lot, with conforming ordinance changes.
states.key_distinction: The statutory definition limits the apparent “each city” duty. Locally chosen unit and zoning goals are not externally allocated need. The 2026 LB839 reporting amendment was vetoed and its override failed.

evidence.reasoning: The act affirmatively requires an action plan and expressly permits integration into a comprehensive plan or a separate plan.
The defined city class/20,000 threshold limits both adoption deadlines; the less-than-50,000 clause is not universal coverage.
The city must submit the demographic analysis and estimates; HUD income definitions are inputs/definitions, not a state housing-needs calculation.
City reports estimate need and city plans set goals; the committee receives them. No external municipal apportionment appears.
Reporting/public-hearing oversight and the explicit middle-housing default after nonadoption are statutory compliance mechanisms.
Official actions establish that the 2026 reporting revision did not become law.

states.plan_mandate: A municipality may create a planning commission. Once established, the commission must prepare and recommend a comprehensive plan; a municipality exercising Chapter 8A zoning authority adopts a comprehensive plan. Joint/regional planning is available with municipal consent.
states.housing_duty: Every Chapter 8A comprehensive plan must include a housing component with goals, plans and programs for current and anticipated residents. This is mandatory plan content within an elective planning/zoning framework, not a universal command for every municipality to adopt a plan.
states.coverage: No population cutoff in the housing-content requirement. It applies throughout the planning commission’s jurisdiction; county, multicounty, regional or joint plans count as a municipality’s plan only with the required municipal consent. A special joint airport-hazard plan under §8A-3-3(f) can exist without a full comprehensive plan.
states.allocation_detail: The preparing local or joint/regional commission projects necessary housing units and sufficient land for its jurisdiction. Chapter 8A does not identify a state or regional total assigned as municipal fair shares; a jointly prepared plan is not by itself an external allocation.
states.assessment_detail: The planning commission preparing the comprehensive plan conducts surveys and studies and analyzes projected housing needs, types and necessary units. The commission may be municipal, county, multicounty, regional or joint; a nonmunicipal plan requires municipal consent to count as the municipal plan.
states.assessment_method: §8A-3-2 requires surveys and studies of existing conditions/services and probable future changes; §8A-3-4 requires projected housing need and unit numbers. These sections prescribe analysis topics, not a uniform state-produced estimate or mathematical allocation formula.
states.assessment_local_role: The municipality can prepare through its own commission or consent to a county/joint/regional plan. Its governing body adopts the plan, and the preparing commission identifies projected need and sufficient land.

contents.detail: Analyze projected needs and housing types for current and anticipated residents, including the number of necessary units.
Housing analysis expressly includes affordable housing; the section does not prescribe income-band quotas.
Identify sufficient land needed for all housing needs alongside projected necessary units. The statute does not specify a parcel-level inventory or detailed zoning-capacity methodology.
Address substandard housing, rehabilitation/improvement of existing housing, and adaptive reuse of buildings.
Analyze universally designed housing accessible to persons with disabilities.
Housing goals, plans and programs sit within a plan with timelines, implementation strategies and financing recommendations.
After adoption the commission must follow the plan, review it and make updates at least every ten years.

states.enforcement: The planning commission recommends the plan to the governing body; plan adoption is part of the statutory zoning pathway. After adoption the commission must follow, review and update the plan at least every ten years. The reviewed provisions contain no state housing-element certification or externally assigned unit-production sanction.
states.key_distinction: West Virginia expressly requires both a housing chapter and projected housing units in a plan, but leaves assessment with the preparing local/joint/regional commission. Optional creation of a commission does not make its housing content optional.

No numerical municipal threshold; consent and special airport-hazard exception are explicit.
Surveys and projected need are assigned to the preparing planning commission, with lawful local or joint/regional pathways.
The unit estimate is for the plan jurisdiction; these provisions identify no higher-level housing total apportioned to municipalities.
Local recommendation/adoption, zoning pathway, and ten-year review are the identified mechanisms.

states.housing_duty: The reviewed state county-planning provisions do not expressly prescribe a separate housing element or a specified housing-needs/site-inventory package. They do require attention to applicable state policies, which include affordable housing objectives; county charters and plans can impose additional housing content.
states.coverage: The relevant local planning units are counties, including the City and County of Honolulu. The state provisions apply to county planning rather than creating a population-triggered duty for independent cities. Section 46-4 excludes specified forest-reserve lands from its zoning framework.
states.allocation_detail: No mandatory state/regional allocation of housing need to county general plans was identified in the reviewed provisions. states.assessment_detail: Sections 46-4 and 226-58 require sound county planning and consideration of state policy, but specify no controlling general-plan housing-demand calculation or assessor. State housing research and functional planning are separate from that scoped finding.
states.assessment_method: County plans use sound rationale, data, analyses and public/agency input. State functional plans are prepared by the responsible state agency with county participation, but the cited law supplies no municipal housing-share formula.
states.assessment_local_role: Counties formulate their plans under their charters, address local needs and consider statewide functional plans. No externally assigned housing-unit number was identified as controlling their general plans.
states.enforcement: Section 46-4 requires zoning within the comprehensive-plan framework and provides county zoning enforcement/appeals; § 226-58 directs county plan formulation and consideration of state functional plans. The reviewed provisions contain no separate housing-element certification or assigned-housing-number enforcement process.
states.key_distinction: Hawaiʻi has state housing objectives and state functional planning, while local planning is county-based. Those features should not be counted automatically as a state-mandated housing element or municipal housing allocation.

evidence.reasoning: The general-plan statutes require coordinated county planning and applicable state-policy consideration, but do not enumerate a mandatory housing component or housing-needs inventory.
The operative planning institutions are counties/city-and-county, with zoning jurisdiction qualifications in § 46-4.
County data/analysis requirements and state functional planning identify general planning responsibilities, not a controlling general-plan housing-demand estimate.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.plan_mandate: Established planning boards must prepare and update master plans. Adopting zoning requires the mandatory vision and land-use sections; housing is expressly an optional section.
states.housing_duty: RSA 674:2 III(l) authorizes a housing section but does not require municipalities to include it. RPCs nevertheless must produce regional housing needs assessments; zoning municipalities separately must provide reasonable and realistic workforce-housing opportunities.
states.coverage: Optional housing section available statewide, without a population trigger. The separate workforce-housing obligation applies to every municipality exercising land-use ordinance/regulation powers.

states.name: Alaska
states.plan_mandate: First- and second-class boroughs must plan under AS 29.40 and adopt a comprehensive plan. First-class cities outside boroughs have the same planning duty; second-class cities outside boroughs may exercise it. Home-rule boroughs and cities outside boroughs have a general planning duty under separate home-rule provisions.
states.housing_duty: Effective October 14, 2025, AS 29.40.030(a) expressly includes a housing development plan among the components that a comprehensive plan may include. Housing remains optional.
states.coverage: The chapter 29.40 framework applies to first-/second-class boroughs and, through AS 29.35.260(c), first-class cities outside boroughs and participating second-class cities outside boroughs. Borough planning is areawide, with authorized delegation to cities. Home-rule planning provisions do not impose the same enumerated chapter 29.40 contents.
states.timing_note: SB 50 became chapter 19 SLA 2025, effective October 14, 2025. The official downloadable Title 29 compilation read on September 20, 2026 omitted its housing addition, so the enacted amendment and official bill history control this record.
states.allocation_detail: The enacted optional housing-development-plan item supplies neither an assessment formula nor an external municipal housing-need assignment. No such assignment was identified in the reviewed Title 29 planning framework.
states.assessment_detail: The reviewed planning provisions identify no required housing-need estimate or assessor. The locality may prepare a housing-development plan, but the statute does not prescribe its analytical contents.
states.assessment_method: No housing-need formula is specified in AS 29.40.030 or the 2025 amendment.
states.assessment_local_role: The local planning commission recommends and the local governing body adopts the comprehensive plan and any chosen housing component; adoption does not require accommodating a state-assigned housing number under these provisions.

contents.detail: A housing development plan is expressly optional; the enacted provision does not enumerate required contents such as need estimates or a sites inventory.

states.enforcement: For chapter 29.40 jurisdictions, the governing body adopts the comprehensive plan by ordinance and periodically reviews and updates it as necessary. These general planning procedures do not convert the optional housing-development component into a mandatory one.
states.key_distinction: The 2025 law added optional housing planning, not a mandatory housing element. Borough/city class and home-rule status matter more than population cutoffs.

Sections 29.35.180 and .260(c) distinguish borough classes, home rule and cities outside boroughs; § 29.40.010 provides areawide planning/delegation.
The optional item contains no required need-estimation task or institutional assignment.

states.name: Vermont
states.plan_mandate: Municipal comprehensive planning is authorized, not universally compelled, by 24 V.S.A. § 4381. A municipality choosing a plan must meet § 4382; regional approval has additional compatibility requirements.
states.housing_duty: An adopted municipal plan must include a housing element addressing the needs and targets identified by its regional planning commission. Act 179 expanded its contents effective July 1, 2026.
states.coverage: Municipal plans statewide, without a population cutoff. The mandate is conditional on undertaking the municipal planning program; regional planning commissions separately must assess regional and community needs.
states.assessment_detail: The Department of Housing and Community Development publishes statewide and regional housing targets or ranges in the Statewide Housing Needs Assessment. Regional planning commissions then assess housing investments and disaggregate regional targets among municipalities, using demographic, stock and local studies.
states.assessment_method: Section 4348a(a)(9) specifies affordability, price, quality, size/type and zoning-district considerations. DHCD supplies the initial state/regional targets; RPCs perform the community-level assessment and disaggregation. The statute does not prescribe a single mathematical municipal formula.
states.assessment_local_role: The municipality supplies local housing information and writes actions responsive to its RPC target. It analyzes regulatory, labor and physical constraints and documents progress when amending or readopting its plan; local plan authorship does not make it the initial need assessor.
states.allocation_authority: Regional planning commissions, from DHCD targets
states.allocation_detail: RPCs must disaggregate the state regional housing targets or ranges by municipality. Municipal housing elements must address those RPC needs and targets. This is externally assigned planning need, without a statutory guarantee of construction or California-style housing-element certification.
states.timing_note: Expanded housing-element contents effective July 1, 2026; online § 4382 alone omits this amendment.

contents.detail: Address RPC housing needs and targets using year-round and seasonal dwelling data.
Include specific actions addressing low- and moderate-income housing needs.
Analyze regulatory, labor and physical constraints on sufficient development, redevelopment and rehabilitation.
Describe public/private actions and what the municipality may do to accommodate projected needs.
Document progress toward construction of needed units and update when the plan is amended or readopted.

states.enforcement: RPC approval checks required elements and compatibility with the regional plan; confirmation requires an approved plan and active implementation. Confirmation brings planning funds and impact-fee authority. These mechanisms do not convert the target into a municipal construction obligation.
states.key_distinction: Municipal plans are optional, but their housing elements respond to external targets. The 2026 session law adds requirements missing from the displayed 2025 code compilation.

states.name: Wyoming
states.plan_mandate: A city or town may establish a planning commission. The commission must prepare and adopt a master plan after public hearings; the governing body may adopt the master plan. The reviewed article does not impose a universal municipal comprehensive-plan adoption duty.
states.housing_duty: The municipal master-plan article does not expressly require a housing element, housing-needs assessment or equivalent municipality-wide housing strategy.
states.coverage: Reviewed scope: cities and towns under Title 15, chapter 1, article 5. Commission planning beyond municipal boundaries requires county-planning concurrence. No housing-specific population trigger is stated in these sections.
states.allocation_detail: No state or regional municipal housing-need allocation was identified in the reviewed municipal planning article. Statewide housing studies and individual housing programs are not coded as an allocation controlling local general plans.
states.assessment_detail: The reviewed municipal planning provisions require general surveys of conditions and probable future growth, but specify no required housing-demand calculation or housing assessor.
states.assessment_method: General careful and comprehensive surveys under § 15-1-504; no housing-need method or formula identified in the reviewed article.
states.assessment_local_role: An established local planning commission surveys and prepares the master plan, and the governing body may adopt it. No externally assigned housing estimate must be accommodated under these provisions.
states.enforcement: The article provides public hearings, commission certification and optional governing-body adoption. After adoption, certain public facilities require commission review for conformity, subject to governing-body override. No housing-element certification or housing-number compliance mechanism was identified in this article.
states.key_distinction: A general zoning plan, population-density recommendations and slum-area replanning are listed master-plan subjects, but they do not expressly require a housing-needs element or sites inventory.

evidence.reasoning: Sections 15-1-502–505 authorize the commission and list master-plan subjects without an express housing element.
The municipal article covers cities/towns; extra-municipal commission territory needs county concurrence.
The general survey instruction in § 15-1-504 does not specify a housing-demand estimate or assessor.
No quantified external municipal housing assignment appears in the reviewed article.
Sections 15-1-503,505,506 establish hearings, adoption and public-facility plan review, rather than housing-specific compliance.
